name: Tan Ngang
ingredients: Local aromatic herbs (like Morok metpa or coriander)
instructions: 1. Clean and cut the duck meat into medium-sized pieces.
2. Heat mustard oil in a heavy-bottomed pan or wok until smoking point, then reduce heat.
3. Add chopped onions, ginger-garlic paste, and green chilies; sauté until golden brown.
4. Add turmeric powder and the duck pieces, searing the meat until it browns on all sides.
5. Add salt and a small amount of water to cover the meat, then cover and simmer over low heat until the meat is tender.
6. Once the liquid has reduced to a thick, flavorful gravy and the meat is succulent, garnish with fresh herbs and serve hot with steamed rice.
description: Tan Ngang is a signature Manipuri delicacy featuring duck meat, which is a prized protein in the region. It is traditionally prepared during special occasions and festivals, reflecting the indigenous culinary practices of the Meitei community that emphasize natural, robust flavors.
